minutes.headline: Select Board heard Vertex's building condition assessments and agreed to plow the full School Street sidewalk meanwhile.
minutes.summary: Vertex presented property condition assessments for Town Hall, Ritter, TC Passios, the old primary school and Brooks House, with board members questioning abatement and demolition costs. The board then worked through its agenda-items list, deciding which items become workshops or agenda items, and took up the sidewalk plowing question, the town manager report and committee reports. Public comment raised cost of the study and bonding capacity, and the board closed by entering executive session.

what_happened.line: The Select Board agreed to plow the full sidewalk from the end of the Mass Ave sidewalk to St. Boniface, while following up with the state and town counsel on liability.
Vertex presented condition assessments for Town Hall, Ritter, TC Passios, the old primary school and Brooks House; the old primary school was rated very poor.

Board members questioned abatement and demolition costs, which Vertex described as conservative estimates based on visual review only, and said repairing all five buildings must come down significantly.
The board sorted its agenda-items list, making social media policy a workshop and Lake Shirley access and BYOB/liquor rules agenda items.
Vertex reports are to be posted on the town website, with Eagle House and Turkey Hill reports expected in two to three weeks.

why_it_matters: The condition assessments are the cost basis for decisions on five town and school buildings, which would likely be paid through taxes or borrowing, so residents may be asked to vote on any project that follows.
A resident asked about the town's bonding capacity and about Vertex's fee, and the minutes do not record a clear answer on either, so how much the town can borrow is still unstated.
watch_next: Vertex reports on Eagle House and Turkey Hill, expected in two to three weeks, and posting of the Vertex reports on the town website.
